summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, COPD, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and chest tightness over five days, following a recent hospitalization for a similar episode. The flare was attributed to acute on chronic systolic heart failure, likely triggered by dietary indiscretion involving high sodium intake. He was treated with intravenous furosemide, transitioned back to oral torsemide, and received supportive care including antibiotics and steroids for presumed infection and COPD exacerbation. His symptoms improved, with resolution of pulmonary edema on imaging, stabilization of renal function, and correction of hyperkalemia. Blood glucose levels normalized after discontinuation of steroids. He was discharged home on his baseline medications with education on low-sodium diet and weight monitoring.
